L00028: L00029: ## 📢 Updates L00030: L00031: - 2024-07-16: We released our [environment and dataset](https://github.com/xlang-ai/Spider2-V), [website](https://spider2-v.github.io/) and [arxiv paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.10956). Check it out! L00032: L00033: ## 🏗️ Installation L00034: ### 💾 On Your Desktop or Server L00035: The executable environment~(desktop Ubuntu 22.04 LTS) is based on our previous work [OSWord](https://github.com/xlang-ai/OSWorld). Please install the pip dependencies and virtual machine first. L00036: L00037: 1. First, clone this repository and `cd` into it. Then, install the dependencies listed in `requirements.txt`. It is recommended that you use the latest version of `conda` to manage the environment, but you can also choose to manually install the dependencies. Please ensure that the version of Python is >= 3.11. L00038: ```bash L00039: # Clone the Spider2-V repository L00040: git clone https://github.com/xlang-ai/Spider2-V L00041: L00042: # Change directory into the cloned repository L00043: cd Spider2-V L00044: L00045: # Optional: Create a Conda environment for Spider2-V L00046: conda create -n spider2v python=3.11 L00047: conda activate spider2v L00048: L00049: # Install required dependencies L00050: pip install -r requirements.txt L00051: ``` L00052: 2. Install [VMware Workstation Pro](https://www.vmware.com/products/workstation-pro/workstation-pro-evaluation.html) (for systems with Apple Chips, you should install [VMware Fusion](https://www.vmware.com/go/getfusion)) and append the `vmrun` command into system path. The installation process can refer to [How to install VMware Worksation Pro](./INSTALL_VMWARE.md). Verify the successful installation by running the following: L00053: ```bash L00054: vmrun -T ws list L00055: ``` L00056: If the installation along with the environment variable set is successful, you will see the message showing the current running virtual machines. L00057: > **Note:** We will also support using [VirtualBox](https://www.virtualbox.org/) in the near future if you have issues with VMware Pro. L00058: L00059: 3. Install other dependencies like Playwright. L00060: ```bash L00061: playwright install chromium L00062: ``` L00063: All set! Now, you/agent can interact with the environment via the [Quick Start](#-quick-start) below. L00064: L00065: L00066: ### 🚀 Quick Start L00067: Run the following minimal example to interact with the environment: L00068: - It will automatically download the prepared virtual machine from Huggingface (for [arm64](https://huggingface.co/datasets/xlangai/ubuntu_spider2v/blob/main/ubuntu-arm.zip) and for [x86](https://huggingface.co/datasets/xlangai/ubuntu_spider2v/blob/main/ubuntu-x86.zip)) into `./vm_data`, configure the environment, and take one snapshot called `init_state` for you. L00069: ```python L00070: from desktop_env.envs.desktop_env import DesktopEnv L00071: L00072: # feel free to change the example! L00073: # task instruction: Help me materialize the asset top10_story_ids in this dagster project in the UI. Do NOT materialize other assets. L00074: example_path = 'evlauation_examples/examples/dagster/22ef9058-6188-422a-9c12-e6934e4ed936/22ef9058-6188-422a-9c12-e6934e4ed936.json' L00075: with open(example_path, 'r') as infile: L00076: example = json.load(infile) L00077: L00078: env = DesktopEnv(action_space="pyautogui") L00079: L00080: obs = env.reset(task_config=example) L00081: print(f'Task instruction: {example["instruction"]}') L00082: obs, reward, done, info = env.step("pyautogui.rightClick()") L00083: input('Now, you can finish the task in the virtual machine manually and Press ENTER to evaluate ...') L00084: score = env.evaluate() L00085: print(f'Evaluation score: {float(score):.1f}') L00086: env.close() L00087: ``` L00088: You will see all the logs of the system running normally, including the successful creation of the environment, completion of setup, and successful execution of a `rightClick` action on the screen, which means you are ready to continue. L00089: L00090: ## 🧪 Experiments L00091: L00092: A quick glance on the success rates of state-of-the-art VLM agents. L00093: L00094: | VLM | Abstract | Verbose | Account | Non-Account | Overall | L00095: | -------------- | -------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- | -------- | L00096: | Claude-3-Opus | 5.3 | 10.9 | 5.9 | 9.3 | 8.1 | L00097: | Gemini-Pro-1.5 | 6.1 | 12.1 | 8.8 | 9.3 | 9.1 | L00098: | GPT-4o | 11.3 | 16.2 | 10.6 | 15.6 | 13.8 | L00099: | GPT-4V | 11.3 | 16.6 | 11.2 | 15.4 | **14.0** | L00100: L00101: ### 🕸️ Different Data Splits L00102: The entire task set contains $494$ examples (`evaluation_examples/test_all.json`) covering $20$ applications. There are different categories to split the entire task set into subsets, depending on: L00103: - whether the task instruction is *verbose* or *abstract* (`evaluation_examples/test_verbose.json` and `evaluation_examples/test_abstract.json`) L00104: - whether a real account is needed (`evaluation_examples/test_account.json` and `evaluation_examples/test_non_account.json`) L00105: - etc. L00106: L00107: Note that, *verbose* instruction means we explicitly tell the agent how to complete the task step-by-step. If you want to test examples which require real accounts (e.g., Snowflake and Google BigQuery), please register relevant accounts and fill credentials into template files under folder `evaluation_examples/settings` first (see [Account Guideline](ACCOUNT_GUIDELINE.md) for more step-by-step details). L00108: L00109: With respect to the task format, see [Task Format](evaluation_examples/README.md#task-format). L00110: L00111: ### 👷 Human Validation L00112: If you want to check more examples manually in the virtual machine on a GUI screen, which includes: L00113: 1. reseting the environment; L00114: 2. completing the task in the virtual machine by yourself; L00115: 3. invoking the customized evaluation function after completion, L00116: you can run the following interactive script: L00117: - if the `--path_to_vm` argument is not specified, the script will automatically find available virtual machines under folder `./vm_data`. If not found, it will download our prepared VM from Huggingface (for [arm64](https://huggingface.co/datasets/xlangai/ubuntu_spider2v/blob/main/ubuntu-arm.zip) and for [x86](https://huggingface.co/datasets/xlangai/ubuntu_spider2v/blob/main/ubuntu-x86.zip)) into `./vm_data` and use it L00118: - if the `--snapshot` argument is not specified, it will use snapshot with name `init_state` by default L00119: - if the `--example` argument is not specified, it will test on one example `evaluation_examples/test_one.json` by default L00120: ```bash L00121: python run_spider2v_human.py --snapshot init_state --example evaluation_examples/test_non_account.json L00122: ``` L00123: L00124: ### 💻 Agent Baselines L00125: If you wish to run the baseline agent used in our paper, you can execute the following command as an example under the GPT4-o pyautogui+SoM+ExecutionFeedback+RAG setting: L00126: L00127: Set **OPENAI_API_KEY** environment variable with your API key: L00128: ```bash L00129: export OPENAI_API_KEY='changme' L00130: ``` L00131: L00132: ```bash L00133: python run_spider2v_agent.py --snapshot init_state \ L00134: --model gpt-4o-2024-05-13 \ L00135: --headless \ L00136: --action_space pyautogui \ L00137: --observation_space som \ L00138: --execution_feedback \ L00139: --rag \ L00140: --result_dir ./results \ L00141: --example evaluation_examples/test_non_account.json L00142: ``` L00143: The results, which include screenshots, a11y trees, actions, and video recordings of the agent's task completion, will be saved in the `./results` directory. L00144: L00145: > If you want to use other models, you can revise the code file `mm_agents/agent.py`. L00146: L00147: L00148: ## ❓ FAQ L00149: ### What is the username and password for the virtual machines? L00150: The username and password for the virtual machines are as follows: L00151: - **Ubuntu:** `user` / `password` L00152: L00153: ### How to tackle task examples requiring accounts? L00154: L00155: See [Account Guideline](ACCOUNT_GUIDELINE.md) L00156: L00157: ### How can I configure a proxy for the VM if I'm behind a GFW? L00158: L00159: See [Proxy Guideline](PROXY_GUIDELINE.md). L00160: L00161: ### Where to download the documents for retrieval? L00162: The preprocessed documents can be downloaded from [GoogleDrive](https://drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=1aGaHXDkBeoUZ9EOIPj7iIRFra_2FjJoZ&export=download&authuser=0&confirm=t). See [Documents](evaluation_examples/documents/README.md) for details. L00163: L00164: ### What are the running times and costs? L00165: | Setting | Expected Time | Average Prompt Tokens | Average Completion Tokens | Average Cost | L00166: | --------| ------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------ | L00167: | GPT-4o | 8.7m | 0.32M | 1.6K | $1.64 | L00168: | GPT-4V | 9.1m | 0.32M | 1.8K | $3.29 | L00169: L00170: - action_space = pyautogui, observation_space = SoM L00171: - history_trajectory_length = 3, max_steps = 15, RAG = True L00172: - prompt tokens include image pixels. Calculated per task in June 2024. L00173: L00174: ## 📄 Citation L00175: If you find this benchmark useful, please consider citing our work: L00176: ``` L00177: @misc{Spider2-V, L00178: title={Spider2-V: How Far Are Multimodal Agents From Automating Data Science and Engineering Workflows?}, L00179: author={Ruisheng Cao and Fangyu Lei and Haoyuan Wu and Jixuan Chen and Yeqiao Fu and Hongcheng Gao and Xinzhuang Xiong and Hanchong Zhang and Yuchen Mao and Wenjing Hu and Tianbao Xie and Hongshen Xu and Danyang Zhang and Sida Wang and Ruoxi Sun and Pengcheng Yin and Caiming Xiong and Ansong Ni and Qian Liu and Victor Zhong and Lu Chen and Kai Yu and Tao Yu}, L00180: year={2024}, L00181: eprint={2407.10956}, L00182: archivePrefix={arXiv}, L00183: primaryClass={cs.AI}, L00184: url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.10956}, L00185: } L00186: ``` L00187: L00188: ``` L00189: @misc{OSWorld, L00190: title={OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments}, L00191: author={Tianbao Xie and Danyang Zhang and Jixuan Chen and Xiaochuan Li and Siheng Zhao and Ruisheng Cao and Toh Jing Hua and Zhoujun Cheng and Dongchan Shin and Fangyu Lei and Yitao Liu and Yiheng Xu and Shuyan Zhou and Silvio Savarese and Caiming Xiong and Victor Zhong and Tao Yu}, L00192: year={2024}, L00193: eprint={2404.07972}, L00194: archivePrefix={arXiv}, L00195: primaryClass={cs.AI} L00196: } L00197: ```

L00009: def get_dbt_profiles(env, config: Dict[str, str]) -> str:
L00010:     """ Download dbt profiles.yml file from VM, search all possible paths and return the first one found.
L00011:     Paths include:
L00012:         config (Dict[str, Any]):
L00013:             dirs (List[str]): a list of possible dirs to search profiles.yml, if the path starts with a '$', it will be treated as an environment variable
L00014:             dest (str): local file name of the downloaded file
L00015:         working, default and environment variable DBT_PROFILES_DIR
L00016:     """
L00017:     for fp in config["dirs"]:
L00018:         if fp.startswith('$'):
L00019:             # fetching ENV vars does not work, because the command below is executed in a new shell in non-login,
L00020:             # non-interactive mode thus, the environment variable is not available
L00021:             fp = get_vm_command_line(env, {"command": ["/bin/bash", "-c", f"echo \"{fp}\""]})
L00022:             if type(fp) == str and fp.strip() != "":
L00023:                 file = get_vm_file(env, {"path": fp.strip() + '/profiles.yml', "dest": config["dest"]})
L00024:                 if file is not None:
L00025:                     return file
L00026:         else:
L00027:             file = get_vm_file(env, {"path": fp + '/profiles.yml', "dest": config["dest"]})
L00028:             if file is not None:
L00029:                 return file
L00030: 
L00031:     return None

L00044:

L00118: def get_dbt_job_info(env, config: Dict[str, str]):
L00119:     """ Retrieve the information on Dbt project job.

L00125:                 prev_name: the name of the job whose completion will trigger the target job
L00126:                 fields (list, required): the specific fields we want to extract for evaluation. Could be:

L00134: 
L00135:     state = subprocess.run(['dbt-cloud', 'project', 'list'],
L00136:                            shell=False, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, timeout=60, text=True,
L00137:                            encoding="utf-8")
L00138:     project_list = json.loads(state.stdout)['data']
L00139:     if len(project_list) == 0:
L00140:         return "None"
L00141:     else:

L00148: 
L00149:     if len(job_list) == 0:

L00151: 
L00152:     result = ""

L00155:     fields = config.get("fields", [])
L00156: 
L00157:     found = False
L00158:     for job in job_list:
L00159:         job_id[job['name']] = job['id']
L00160:         if job['name'] == name:
L00161:             found = True
L00162:             for field in fields:
L00163:                 if field.startswith('time_'):
L00164:                     schedule = job['schedule']['time']
L00165:                     time_type = field[5:]
L00166:                     result += str(schedule[time_type])
L00167:                 elif field == "job_completion_trigger_condition":
L00168:                     if job[field] is None:
L00169:                         return "None"
L00170:                     condition = job[field]['condition']
L00171:                     prev_name = config.get("prev_name", "New Job")
L00172:                     if condition['job_id'] == job_id[prev_name]:
L00173:                         result += "matched "
L00174:                     else:
L00175:                         result += "mismatched "
L00176:                     for status in condition['statuses']:
L00177:                         result += str(status) + ' '
L00178:                 else:
L00179:                     result += str(job[field])
L00180:                 result += ' '
L00181: 
L00182:     if not found:
L00183:         return "None"
L00184:     return result

L00031: def get_local_file(env, config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
L00032:     """ File is already on the local host machine.
L00033:     Config:
L00034:         path (str): absolute path on the local machine
L00035:         dest (str): file name to be copied into the cache dir, by default, use the base name of the path
L00036:     """
L00037:     path = config["path"]
L00038:     dest = config.get('dest', os.path.basename(path))
L00039:     dest = os.path.join(env.cache_dir, dest)
L00040:     if not os.path.exists(path):
L00041:         logger.error(f'[ERROR]: The specified file path {path} is not found on the local machine!')
L00042:         return
L00043:     
L00044:     if os.path.isdir(path): # recursively copy the directory (overwrite if exists)
L00045:         if os.path.exists(dest) and os.path.isdir(dest):
L00046:             shutil.rmtree(dest)
L00047:         shutil.copytree(path, dest, dirs_exist_ok=True)
L00048:     else: # directly copy the file (overwrite if exists)
L00049:         shutil.copyfile(path, dest)
L00050:     return dest

L00053: def get_cloud_file(env, config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Union[str, List[str]]:
L00054:     """
L00055:     Config:
L00056:         path (str|List[str]): the url to download from
L00057:         dest (str|List[str])): file name of the downloaded file
L00058:         multi (bool) : optional. if path and dest are lists providing
L00059:           information of multiple files. defaults to False
L00060:         gives (List[int]): optional. defaults to [0]. which files are directly
L00061:           returned to the metric. if len==1, str is returned; else, list is
L00062:           returned.
L00063:     """
L00064: 
L00065:     if not config.get("multi", False):
L00066:         paths: List[str] = [config["path"]]
L00067:         dests: List[str] = [config["dest"]]
L00068:     else:
L00069:         paths: List[str] = config["path"]
L00070:         dests: List[str] = config["dest"]
L00071:     cache_paths: List[str] = []
L00072: 
L00073:     gives: Set[int] = set(config.get("gives", [0]))
L00074: 
L00075:     for i, (p, d) in enumerate(zip(paths, dests)):
L00076:         _path = os.path.join(env.cache_dir, d)
L00077:         if i in gives:
L00078:             cache_paths.append(_path)
L00079: 
L00080:         if os.path.exists(_path):
L00081:             #return _path
L00082:             continue
L00083: 
L00084:         url = p
L00085:         response = requests.get(url, stream=True)
L00086:         response.raise_for_status()
L00087: 
L00088:         with open(_path, 'wb') as f:
L00089:             for chunk in response.iter_content(chunk_size=8192):
L00090:                 if chunk:
L00091:                     f.write(chunk)
L00092: 
L00093:     return cache_paths[0] if len(cache_paths)==1 else cache_paths
L00094:

L00096: def get_vm_file(env, config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Union[Optional[str], List[Optional[str]]]:
L00097:     """
L00098:     Config:
L00099:         path (str): absolute path on the VM to fetch
L00100:         dest (str): file name of the downloaded file
L00101:         multi (bool) : optional. if path and dest are lists providing
